scene.name: THE CLOCK — Kelly (1944) cited going train, spring-driven, pendulum-gated, real involute teeth (module [estimated])

ceramic_alumina.mechanism: wide-gap insulator: no visible absorber -> white
ceramic_alumina.density_method: tabulated (no derivable cell: amorphous / complex / missing)

plugs.description: arbors, pendulum pivot and hour-hand axis held as if by clock plates (plates/pillars/dial rendered below, not structurally simulated)

choices.reason: no brass entry exists in the table; real clock wheels are brass and pinions hardened steel (the opposite hardness split from what's used here) — steel_mild is the closer real-world match for both roles and was never compared before picking iron/copper for color contrast alone

choices.description: gear pressure angle (deg) and face width (m)
choices.reason: 20 deg is the modern ISO/AGMA standard, picked over the historically-plausible 14.5 deg alternative for a 1940s train; face width sized to look proportionate at the estimated module
choices.checked: blueprint kelly_1944 spec's pressure_angle_deg and face_width_mm fields (both null — same GEOMETRY_GAP class as module)

choices.description: mainspring stiffness k and initial wound angle (rad), pendulum bob mass (kg)
choices.reason: tuned empirically for a ~60s watchable run duration; pendulum mass is a plausible small-clock figure with nothing in the catalog to check it against
choices.checked: dynamics/mechanisms/spring.py (MVP linear Hooke's-law model, no cited real mainspring curve — solid unspoked wheels here are also heavier than a real movement's, so the constant is sized to THIS build, not a real spring)

choices.description: pendulum pivot placement (height above arbor row, z offset in mesh-plane pitches) and release angle (deg)
choices.reason: pure layout geometry clearing the escape arbor and gear planes; a real movement's back-cock position isn't modeled or cited. Release angle is a small-angle demo pick with no cited amplitude
cosmetic proportions relative to the dial that also set the hour hand's own moment of inertia; not sourced
choices.checked: none exists — no blueprint/catalog covers clock-hand dimensions; hand_m also breaks this function's own mass-from-density*volume pattern used by every other body

choices.reason: closest available match to a real dial's ivory/enamel face; no dedicated enamel entry exists in the materials table

scene.source: Going train teeth CITED: Kelly, A Practical Course in Horology (1944) pp.16-18 via blueprint/catalog (each gear leaf carries its own citation). DERIVED: pendulum L=0.2385 m from the cited 600:1 escape:center ratio + anchor cadence (NOT Kelly's lever double-impulse). ESTIMATED: module (no module cited — GEOMETRY_GAP), pressure angle, spring constants, solid (unspoked) wheels. No drive plugged (the spring is present, modeled machinery). PLUGGED SUPPORT: arbors, pendulum pivot and hour-hand axis held as if by clock plates (plates/pillars/dial rendered below, not structurally simulated) CHOSEN: wheel material (iron) / pinion material (copper) = ['iron', 'copper'] (checked: sigma_ground.field.interface.surface.MATERIALS (25 entries); alternatives: steel_mild, nickel, titanium; no brass entry exists in the table; real clock wheels are brass and pinions hardened steel (the opposite hardness split from what's used here) — steel_mild is the closer real-world match for both roles and was never compared before picking iron/copper for color contrast alone) CHOSEN: gear pressure angle (deg) and face width (m) = [20.0, 0.006] (checked: blueprint kelly_1944 spec's pressure_angle_deg and face_width_mm fields (both null — same GEOMETRY_GAP class as module); alternatives: 14.5; 20 deg is the modern ISO/AGMA standard, picked over the historically-plausible 14.5 deg alternative for a 1940s train; face width sized to look proportionate at the estimated module) CHOSEN: mainspring stiffness k and initial wound angle (rad), pendulum bob mass (kg) = [0.12, 30.0, 0.05] (checked: dynamics/mechanisms/spring.py (MVP linear Hooke's-law model, no cited real mainspring curve — solid unspoked wheels here are also heavier than a real movement's, so the constant is sized to THIS build, not a real spring); tuned empirically for a ~60s watchable run duration; pendulum mass is a plausible small-clock figure with nothing in the catalog to check it against) CHOSEN: pendulum pivot placement (height above arbor row, z offset in mesh-plane pitches) and release angle (deg) = [0.12, -3.5, 6.0] (pure layout geometry clearing the escape arbor and gear planes; a real movement's back-cock position isn't modeled or cited. Release angle is a small-angle demo pick with no cited amplitude) CHOSEN: hand mass (kg) and lengths (m): hour/minute = [0.01, 0.035, 0.055] (checked: none exists — no blueprint/catalog covers clock-hand dimensions; hand_m also breaks this function's own mass-from-density*volume pattern used by every other body; cosmetic proportions relative to the dial that also set the hour hand's own moment of inertia; not sourced) CHOSEN: clock dial material = 'ceramic_alumina' (checked: sigma_ground.field.interface.surface.MATERIALS (25 entries); alternatives: aluminum, iron, copper, bone, glass; closest available match to a real dial's ivory/enamel face; no dedicated enamel entry exists in the materials table)
